evidence_quotes.quote: Se aplicaron dos encuestas con dos muestreos aleatorios estratificados (Mukherjee et al., 2022) a una población finita de 88,686 usuarios del SEAPAL-VALLARTA (SEAPAL, 2023).

El primer muestreo a usuarios domésticos, doméstico residencial, Comerciales e Industriales (D.C.I.) y el segundo, a usuarios hoteleros con una muestra de 364 usuarios D.C.I. y 100 usuarios hoteleros.

Los artículos 4, 9, 14, 16, 18, 46, 51 y 58 del RPSPAPDATDARMPV establecen contribuciones y pagos de derechos que deberá realizar la población para solicitar la contratación de los servicios, cubrir las cuotas por la conexión a las redes e instalación de tomas y dictamen de factibilidad, así como la adhesión al contrato con el organismo operador para la prestación de los servicios.

La asequibilidad de las tarifas se promueve a su vez con las disposiciones del capítulo VII del RPSPAPDATDARMPV, que establecen subsidios para instituciones de asistencia social y uso doméstico, sin que estos rebasen el 50% de los costos del consumo y previo el cumplimiento de requisitos correspondientes, como se señala en la tabla 4.
Aun cuando el 60% de los usuarios D.C.I. manifiestan que el costo es accesible, se tiene al 38% que afirman costos elevados con 137 usuarios en este último porcentaje

el 66.20% de los usuarios D.C.I. se sienten seguros de contar con agua al hacer el pago por el suministro y 33.80% de estos usuarios afirman que dicho pago no les asegura el poder disponer del recurso hídrico.

criterion_notes.c1: Examines access to municipal drinking water and wastewater/sanitation services provided by the public utility SEAPAL-VALLARTA in Puerto Vallarta, Jalisco, Mexico, covering domestic, residential domestic, commercial, industrial, and hotel users.
criterion_notes.c2: Satisfies BOTH the plain wording of Criterion 2 and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading. Under the plain wording, it analyzes federal, state, and municipal water legislation and utility regulation. Under the narrow 2026-10-13 reading, it directly examines rule-type mechanisms governing service access and affordability: (1) statutory and municipal regulatory rules on connection fees, feasibility assessments, and service contracting (RPSPAPDATDARMPV arts. 4, 9, 14, 16, 18, 44, 46, 51, 52, 57, 58 and Ley de Ingresos de Puerto Vallarta 2025 art. 56), (2) volumetric tariff structures (minimum quota, increasing block, and total cost regimes), and (3) domestic tariff subsidy caps (up to 50%) and eligibility screening requirements including citizenship, property ownership or tenancy, residency, payment standing, income requirements, and a 60 m3 bimonthly consumption ceiling (RPSPAPDATDARMPV ch. VII, Table 4).
criterion_notes.c3: Contains primary empirical survey evidence combined with socio-legal regulatory analysis: two stratified random sample surveys drawn from a finite population of 88,686 SEAPAL-VALLARTA users (n = 364 domestic, residential domestic, commercial, and industrial users selected across colonias via QGIS, and n = 100 hotel users from a utility list), analyzed with descriptive statistics and contingency tables in SPSS 2021.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports empirical outcomes directly relevant to affordability, tariff burden/consumption block placement, connection cost schedules, and perceived reliability/security of water supply upon payment (e.g., 38% of D.C.I. users report elevated tariff costs; 89.83% of D.C.I. users fall into increasing-cost tariff ranges; 33.80% of D.C.I. users vs. 9% of hotel users report that paying for service does not ensure water availability).
criterion_notes.c5: Population and unit of analysis (SEAPAL-VALLARTA utility user accounts/respondents in Puerto Vallarta, N = 88,686; stratified random samples n = 364 D.C.I. users and n = 100 hotel users), exposure (statutory economic-valuation, connection-fee, volumetric block-tariff, and subsidy-eligibility rules), outcome (approximate tariff payments, perceived tariff affordability, and perceived supply security upon payment), and study design (cross-sectional socio-legal survey and regulatory analysis) are all clearly identified. Note that domestic, residential domestic, commercial, and industrial users are pooled in several D.C.I. percentage summaries, though disaggregated counts by user type are plotted in Figures 3, 5, 6, and 7.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is in Spanish (with an English title and abstract on PDF pages 1-2). Per Inclusion Criterion 10, non-English/Portuguese/Dutch studies are eligible when translation is feasible and the study is potentially important; translation directly from the clean Spanish full text is straightforward, and the translator and translation method should be logged in extraction_note during data extraction.

study_design: Cross-sectional mixed socio-legal regulatory analysis and stratified random user survey (described by authors as a cross-sectional study with qualitative approach analyzed with descriptive statistics and contingency tables in SPSS)
population_and_sample: Users of the municipal drinking water and sewerage utility SEAPAL-VALLARTA in Puerto Vallarta, Jalisco, Mexico (finite population N = 88,686 user accounts), sampled via two stratified random surveys: n = 364 domestic, residential domestic, commercial, and industrial (D.C.I.) users and n = 100 hotel users (unit of analysis: utility user / survey respondent)
exposure: Federal, state, and municipal legal and regulatory rules governing the economic valuation of water, utility service contracting and connection fees, volumetric block tariffs (minimum quota, increasing cost, total cost), and domestic tariff subsidy eligibility criteria (Ley de Aguas Nacionales, Ley Federal de Derechos, LAEJM, Ley de Ingresos del Municipio de Puerto Vallarta 2025, and RPSPAPDATDARMPV)
outcome: Approximate user tariff payments and volumetric tariff-tier placement, user-perceived affordability of drinking water and sanitation tariffs, and user-perceived security/reliability of water supply upon payment
rationale: This Spanish-language socio-legal empirical study meets all inclusion criteria under both the plain wording and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading of Criterion 2. It analyzes concrete municipal and statutory rules governing drinking water and sanitation access in Puerto Vallarta, Mexico—specifically service contracting and connection fees, volumetric tariff structures (minimum, increasing-block, and total-cost regimes), and domestic subsidy eligibility rules (including tenure, citizenship, residency, income, payment-standing, and consumption-cap requirements)—alongside primary stratified random survey data from 364 domestic/commercial/industrial utility users and 100 hotel users reporting tariff burdens, perceived affordability, and perceived supply security. Translation from Spanish is directly feasible per Inclusion Criterion 10.
